result.title: A marine expedition found 31 new species in 2 weeks using breakthrough tech
result.description:
A research mission set out from Brazil to explore the ocean’s ‘twilight zone’. Plunging from 200 to 1,000 metres deep, this is the largest #habitat on Earth and is estimated to contain 90% of the global biosphere.

Researchers on the Schmidt Ocean Institute vessel brought a groundbreaking microscope called the Squid, which uses lasers to scan living creatures - even single-celled ones.

The ocean could hold as many as 1.75 million undescribed #species. But habitat destruction, pollution, climate change, and overfishing all pose grave threats to ocean life.

Friends of Ocean Action is a group of leaders from business, science and civil society who use their knowledge to help conserve the #ocean and sustainably manage marine resources.

result.title: What Makes A Peace Deal Work & How To Get Rid Of Workslop  | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - How to handle AI anxiety at work: 
New tools such as AI are rapidly changing the world of work. So what’s the best way to mitigate FOBO - ‘fear of becoming obsolete’? Here, three chief health officers and medical advisors - Paul Litchfield of Compass Group, Ranit Mishori of the World Bank and Andreas Tautz of DHL - share their suggestions for how to maintain employee mental #health and satisfaction.

03:58 - What makes a peace deal work?: 
What does it take to build a lasting peace? Here to answer the question is Itonde Kakoma, President and CEO of Interpeace. He discusses the worrying rise in conflict worldwide, the role of the private sector in cementing #peace, and why most peace deals fail.

08:10 - How to get rid of workslop: 
Have you ever received poor-quality AI-generated content at work? This is ‘workslop’. 40% of US workers say they have been sent #workslop, according to a survey by BetterUp and Stanford Social Media Lab. And as bringing a piece of workslop up to scratch can take around two hours, it’s costing businesses in lost productivity. Here, Alexi Robichaux, CEO of BetterUp, explains the problem, alongside some solutions.

10:04 - AI is helping Saudi Arabia go solar: 
Saudi Arabia plans to generate half its electricity from renewables by 2030. Studies suggest rooftop solar could provide 40% of Riyadh's energy needs, but high installation costs could hamper the rollout. Now, OptimalPV is using satellite imagery and AI to design solar arrays tailored to individual buildings - an approach it says can cut costs by up to 80%.

result.title: The next tech shift is already here
result.description:
We've spent decades making new technologies bigger. But the next wave of #tech may be heading in the opposite direction. 

The World Economic Forum’s new Top 10 Emerging Technologies Report reveals a surprising pattern emerging across this year's breakthrough innovations:

#Energy systems powered by parked cars and buildings
#Medicines tailored to a single person
#Innovations that are becoming more local, distributed and personal

Hear from Kimmy Bettinger, who leads the report, as she unpacks the trends behind this year's most important emerging technologies. You can find about more about them in the report:  https://www.weforum.org/publications/top-10-emerging-technologies-of-2026

result.title: Summer Davos 2026 Highlights
result.description:
How do we turn today's technological breakthroughs into tomorrow's growth, jobs and opportunity?

That was the question at the heart of the 17th Annual Meeting of the New Champions known as #SummerDavos, where 1,500 leaders from business, government and academia gathered in Dalian, China.

This film captures the conversations, ideas and energy of the meeting, featuring insights from World Economic Forum Managing Directors on shared challenges - from AI to advanced manufacturing, clean energy to the investments needed to accelerate innovation at scale.

result.title: The Hormuz shock, AI and China: the state of global energy, with Jason Bordoff
result.description:
Is 2026 the year it all changed for energy?

The Strait of Hormuz closure was "the largest oil supply disruption in history" but has not (yet) brought the global economy to its knees. But are we now living in a post-Hormuz world where countries and companies are seeking to diversify energy supply and ramp up renewables?

Jason Bordoff of the Center on Global Energy Policy and the Columbia Energy Exchange podcast returns to Radio Davos, at the Forum's 'Summer Davos' in China, for an update on the global energy situation.
Co-hosted by Roberto Booca, head of the Forum's Centre for Energy and Materials.
